architecture.title: vLLM on DGX Spark — one container, one memory slice, one OpenAI port
architecture.caption: Clients (curl, the openai SDK, LiteLLM, NAT, the labs) call the OpenAI-compatible API on :8000. Inside the container the scheduler joins new requests into the running batch (continuous batching). Weights and KV cache pages (PagedAttention) share the slice set by --gpu-memory-utilization, taken from the Spark's 128 GB unified memory. For models larger than one Spark, a Ray cluster over QSFP splits every layer across two Sparks (tensor parallel 2).

sequence.title: Lab 05-4 — one tool-calling round trip through vLLM
sequence.caption: The server's --tool-call-parser turns the model's own syntax into the OpenAI tool_calls field. The lab runs the tool itself (a fake sensor), returns the result as a role=tool message, and the model answers from it. Without --enable-auto-tool-choice the first call fails or returns text only.

charts.title: Full-length 32K sequences that fit — Qwen3-32B NVFP4
charts.caption: From lab 05-1 (arithmetic, not a measurement): (util × 128 GB − 18.4 GB weights − 4 GB runtime) ÷ KV per 32K sequence. fp8 KV doubles the users; raising utilization takes memory from the OS on a unified-memory Spark.

charts.title: Laptop stand-in: total vs per-stream tok/s (Ollama, gemma3:4b)
charts.caption: Measured by lab 05-3 on this Mac against Ollama (LAPTOP STAND-IN, shared with other programs, not a Spark and not vLLM). Here the total did not grow: requests queued. Run the lab against vLLM on your Spark and compare the shape of the curve, never the numbers.
